result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-026.md for WF02-REQ-026 (T-24h 'Still coming?' reconfirmation and T-3h route/QR reminder jobs) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-026, commit 3328a58. Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out (new apps/bot/src/domain/reminders.ts, apps/bot/src/scheduler/reminderJobs.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/reminder24h.ts; changes to domain/notification.ts, domain/registration.ts, domain/event.ts, scheduler/rateLimiter.ts, handlers/withdraw.ts, index.ts, i18n catalogs) is real behavioral surface -- two real scheduled jobs sending real Telegram messages/photos with buttons, a real reconfirm/decline authorization surface, a real cross-process restart scenario. Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read core-directives.md, WF-02 Step 3, qa_testing_guide.md, docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-025.md as reference shape, docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md in full, and the real implementations directly: domain/reminders.ts, scheduler/reminderJobs.ts, handlers/reminder24h.ts, domain/registration.ts's decideReconfirmOutcome/reconfirmRegistration, domain/event.ts's findDoorsAgendaItem/buildEventCardContent. Also read BACKEND-DEV's 21 already-committed tests across reminder24h.test.ts, reminderJobs.db.test.ts, registration.db.test.ts's REQ-026 sections, event.test.ts's findDoorsAgendaItem section, and notification.test.ts's ComposedMessage/sendPhoto additions, plus SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-02c handoff describing 3 scratch adversarial tests it wrote, ran, and deleted (not committed) -- so every case below is independently parameterized against what actually exists, not a duplicate.

Per-AC design, with independence stated explicitly in the spec:
- AC1/AC2/AC4(part)/AC5/AC10: existing committed cases already target these precisely and correctly -- spec cites the exact `-t` filtered re-run for each rather than inventing a duplicate case, and adds one genuinely new case each for AC2 (confirm-after-decline order-of-operations, not covered by either committed file) and AC4 (mid-flight withdrawal landing specifically inside sendLedgeredNotification's composeMessage recheck gap, distinct from the committed 'withdrawn before job runs' case which only exercises the selection-time filter).
- AC3: designed a genuine two-OS-process kill/restart harness (scratch-verify-req026-p1.ts/-p2.ts, npx tsx, fresh Pool/drizzle per process) because no committed test exercises a real process boundary -- confirmed reminderJobs.db.test.ts's own header comment explicitly defers AC3 to 'the genuine two-process kill scripts,' which do not exist as committed files (git status clean, no apps/bot/scratch-* present). Kill point constructed per REQ-025 AC1's own precedent: process 1 calls makeReminder24hJob(...).run(evaluationTime).then(() => process.exit(0)), so the kill lands strictly after the one candidate's sender.send() has already resolved and durably written the delivery log. This also transitively re-proves REQ-025's ledger property holds when reached through a real job's run() entrypoint, which REQ-025's own committed tests never exercise.
- AC7: own fixture, deliberately different from BACKEND-DEV's (America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires vs their Asia/Tashkent; doors at 2026-11-05T21:45:00Z labeled 'Registration & drinks' vs their 2026-09-01T01:30:00Z 'Doors open'; lang 'en' vs 'ru'), with a real exact-substring `===` equality assertion (not `.toContain` alone) between the caption's extracted doors line and buildEventCardContent's own agendaLines entry -- stated explicitly why an independent timezone/value pair is needed for this to be a genuine second proof rather than a re-run of the same inputs.
- AC8: own agenda-kind values ('workshop'/'afterparty') deliberately different from BACKEND-DEV's ('networking'/'close'), confirming findDoorsAgendaItem's kind==='doors' check is a real equality test rather than something that happens to also reject that one particular pair of strings; additionally asserts the two non-doors items' OWN formatted times are absent from the caption (not just the doors label string), closing a gap BACKEND-DEV's own AC8 case does not check.
- AC9: scoped git grep (doors_at / doorsAt across apps/bot only, migration-count check) confirming no such column exists anywhere, per decisions/0007.
- Forged-callback non-authorization: designed as a new PERMANENT committed test file (apps/bot/src/handlers/reminder24h.forgery.test.ts, own nextTgId=990_000_000 range, distinct from every existing counter in the codebase per a grep -rn check across all *.test.ts files), covering the same property SECURITY-REVIEWER verified ad hoc and then deleted (per its own step-02c account) -- an attacker with no registration forging a confirm naming a victim's registrationId, and a separate attacker WITH their own registration forging a decline naming a victim's registrationId instead of their own. Both assert the non-disclosing refusedNotFound reply, zero state change on the victim's row, zero audit rows, and (second case) the attacker's own row also untouched -- ruling out a silent-substitution bug a coarser check could miss.

Stated ISS-0014's --no-file-parallelism requirement, with AC3's own sequential-process-exit correctness note (p1 must visibly exit before p2 starts) restated as part of the test's own construction, matching REQ-025 AC1's precedent.

Gap found while reading: the forged-callback property (a brand-new authorization surface introduced by this requirement) had no permanent regression coverage prior to this spec -- SECURITY-REVIEWER's own adversarial tests were scratch and deleted per its handoff's explicit account. This spec closes that gap with a committed test rather than leaving it as a one-off manual verification. No implementation defect found in domain/reminders.ts, scheduler/reminderJobs.ts, handlers/reminder24h.ts, or the registration.ts/event.ts additions while reading them directly -- nothing to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
